neighbours.label: Inside a quoted spoken command: the words right after the imperative verb (said, “Close your eyes…”, “Turn around and…”); narrated actions and quoted statements stay quiet
fire: The magician covered the box and said, “Shut your eyes and think of a card.”
The instructor stood behind her and said, “Turn around and face the mirror.”
The old woman pointed to the hills and said, “Look up and you will see the path.”
The dentist adjusted the lamp and said, “Open your mouth and stay still.”
He patted the sofa and said, “Lie back and rest for a while.”
The captain raised his hand and said, “Step forward and state your name.”
Her grandfather handed her the shell and said, “Hold it to your ear and listen.”
The priest smiled and said, “Bow your head and close your eyes.”
quiet: The magician covered the box and she shut her eyes and thought of a card.
She turned around and faced the mirror while the instructor watched.
The old woman looked up at the hills and saw the path.
The dentist adjusted the lamp and said, “Your teeth are in good shape.”
He sat on the sofa and said, “I rested for a while this morning.”
The captain raised his hand and said, “The ship leaves at dawn.”
Her grandfather held the shell to his ear and listened.
The priest smiled and said, “The church was built long ago.”

notes: Probes: “Close your eyes and count” 0.76, “Turn around and breathe” 0.59, 'told him to ... look away' 0.31, “Put your hands” 0.22, “Come closer and listen” 0.20, “Go get your coat” 0.15; narrated 'closed his eyes' 0.04, quoted statement 0.04. Middling strength, so the median may fall short.
